blockNote: Scanline-band HDMA thinker driven by parallax_scroll_table (Bank 00, 47245-48013). One spawn = one HDMA channel that rewrites a single PPU register per scanline band every frame. Despite the name, only some table entries scroll a background: others stream COLDATA / CGADSUB / CGDATA colour values or a WH0/WH1 window rectangle through the same band format.
=== SPAWN AND FRAME FLOW ===

thinker-def <#04,#08>: the filter word is $0804, so bit 2 puts it in RunThinkers_TypeB. That pass runs every frame right after ResetHdmaState, so the channel binding is redone every frame. The spawn-record parameter byte (animScratch+2) is the INDEX into parallax_scroll_table (37 word pointers, $00-$24).
1. Entry (once): ParallaxClearHdmaScratch zeroes the 24 band accumulators at $0720-$074F and chatPtr is set to 0.

2. SetEntryHere, then every frame: chatPtr is copied to the global word $0012 and incremented (a frame counter whose bit 0 picks the buffer half), ParallaxBuildHdmaTable rewrites the whole table, and SetupHdmaChannel_Direct binds it to the B-bus register from the entry config (A = register index << 8 | bank $7E, Y = table start). The thinker then leaves $0060 = 1 and $005E = 0.
=== TABLE ENTRY FORMAT (parallax_scroll_table) ===
| Offset | Meaning |
| +0 word | WRAM buffer address in bank $7E. Even frames build there, odd frames at +$0200 (double buffer: the HDMA channel reads the half written last frame) |
| +2 byte | Bank $7E |
| +3 byte | Config: bits 0-5 = B-bus register index n ($2100 + n; also the index into hdma_channel_config); bit 6 ($40) = camera delta x16; bit 7 ($80) = swap the scroll sources (below) |
| +4 byte | Record size: 4 = constant band, 8 = scroll band, 9 = window rectangle |
| +5 ... | Records, ended by a zero height word (size 4 / 8) or a word with bit 15 set (size 9). An entry that is just $FFFF is unused |
Buffers: $7000, $7400, $7800, $7C00, $8000 and $8400, 1 KB each (two $200 halves). Scenes with two or more parallax thinkers (2B, 2D, 2E, 2F, DF, E0, E3) give them different buffers.
=== SCROLL SOURCES AND STRIDE ===

Default: $18 = bg1ScrollH ($068A, BG1 horizontal scroll) as the multiplicand for proportional bands, and $1C = effectScrollV ($0690, BG2 vertical scroll) as the vertical position that the band heights are measured against. With config bit 7 the sources become $18 = effectScrollH ($068C, BG2 horizontal) and $1C = mapScrollV ($068E, BG1 vertical). $1A = effectDeltaX ($06E4, this frame's camera X delta), shifted left 4 times with config bit 6.

ParallaxResolveChannelSpeed sets $04 = parallax_speed_config[hdma_channel_config[n] & 7]. That byte is the HDMA ENTRY STRIDE (count byte plus data): 2 for transfer mode 0 (one byte) and 3 for modes 1 and 2 (one word). It is not a speed. The band writers advance the buffer pointer $62 by $04 per entry.
=== RECORD TYPES ===

Size 4 (colour bands): {height word, value word}. The height is a NEGATIVE line count. $1C accumulates the heights; bands whose running sum is still >= 0 lie above the visible area and are skipped. The first band that makes the sum negative starts the table with |sum| lines; later bands use |height|. Each band is written as count byte (at most $7F lines per HDMA entry, longer bands are split) plus the 1 or 2 value bytes. The value word is read from record +2.

Size 8 (scroll bands): {height word, accumulator pointer, factor word, base word}. The accumulator pointer addresses a word in $0720-$0760. Factor <> 0: MulDivide(A = factor, Y = $18) = (factor low byte x $18) / factor high byte, plus base. This is fixed point with 4 fractional bits: factor $0108 is x0.5 and $0110 is x1.0 of the scroll value, $010E is x0.875. Factor = 0: accumulator += base + $1A, an auto-scroll of base/16 pixels per frame that also follows the camera delta. The value stored per HDMA entry is the accumulator >> 4 with the sign extended from bit 11. Bands above the visible area still update their accumulator; bands below the 224-line budget are not processed.

Size 9 (window rectangles, register $2126/$2127 pair WH0/WH1): {x, width, y, height} in map pixels. Each rectangle is converted against bg1ScrollH and mapScrollV into a WH0 (left) / WH1 (right) byte pair. Lines between rectangles get the value $0000. Horizontally a rectangle is skipped when it starts at column $FF or beyond, ends left of the screen, or starts left of the screen and its right edge is at column $FF or beyond; otherwise the right edge is clamped to $FF. Vertically it is skipped when its top is at line $FF or beyond or, if it starts above the screen, when its bottom is at or above line 0 or at line $FF or beyond. The table ends with one more $0000 line.

=== QUIRKS ===

- The accumulator clear covers only $0720-$074F, but entry $05 uses accumulators up to $0758 and entry $24 up to $0760. Those extra words are never cleared by this thinker. $0720 is also used by sE7_space_bg_scroll and the F7 credits code, so this region is shared.
- A table that covers fewer than 224 lines ends with an explicit count-0 byte; the PPU register then simply keeps the last value written for the rest of the frame.
- The window path hard-codes a 3-byte stride, which only matches register pair WH0/WH1 (mode 1).
- All reads of the table use absolute addressing under DBR $81, which mirrors ROM bank 01.
- Runtime behaviour of the individual entries (what the screen looks like) was not checked; see the questions file.

code_00B88D: Thinker body. Runs once to clear the accumulators, then loops through SetEntryHere every frame: build the table, bind the channel. See the block note for the entry format.
ParallaxClearHdmaScratch: Zeroes the 24 words $0720-$074F that hold the per-band scroll accumulators. Called only at spawn, so accumulators persist (and keep running) across frames. Entries that use more than 24 accumulators (types $05 and $24) are not fully covered.
ParallaxBuildHdmaTable: Rewrites the whole HDMA table for the entry chosen by the spawn parameter. Switches D to 0 (restored from the stacked X at every exit) so $00-$26 are global scratch: $00 = record size then stride, $02 = register index, $04 = entry stride, $08 = lines emitted (window path), $0E = lines left in the current band, $10 = lines still to fill (starts at 224), $18 = scroll multiplicand, $1A = camera delta, $1C = vertical position, $20-$26 = window working values, $5E / $60 = table start / bank for the HDMA bind, $62 / $64 = write pointer.
Dispatches on the record size: 4 = loc_00B98E, 9 = loc_00B9B3, anything else (8) = loc_00B966.
loc_00B966: Scroll-band records (size 8). Walks the records; a band whose running height sum is still non-negative is above the screen and only updates its accumulator (ParallaxApplyScrollOffset). The first band that crosses into the visible area jumps to ParallaxWriteNegativeScrollRamp, which emits it and every following band.
loc_00B98E: Constant-band records (size 4). Skips bands above the screen, then ParallaxWriteNegativeScrollRampY emits the rest.
loc_00B9B3: Window-rectangle records (size 9). Each rectangle is clipped against bg1ScrollH / mapScrollV and, if visible, emitted by ParallaxWriteWindowHdmaEntry. A negative x word ends the list, after which one final $0000 line and the terminator are written.
ParallaxWriteWindowHdmaEntry: Converts one visible rectangle into $24 (first line), $26 (line count) and a WH0/WH1 word (left in the low byte, right in the high byte, right clamped to $FF). A rectangle partly above the screen starts at line 0 with the visible part of its height; one that starts left of the screen gets WH0 = 0.
ParallaxFillHdmaRampRow: Emits the gap between the previous rectangle and this one (value $0000) and then the rectangle's own lines (the window word in Y). Counts are split into HDMA entries of at most $7F lines and $08 tracks the total. The 3-byte stride is hard-coded.
ParallaxResolveChannelSpeed: Looks up hdma_channel_config[register index] & 7 (the DMAP transfer mode), then parallax_speed_config[mode] into $04. The result is the byte stride of one HDMA entry (count + data): 2 for mode 0, 3 for modes 1 and 2. It is a stride, not a speed.
ParallaxWriteNegativeScrollRamp: Emits scroll bands (size 8) starting at the current record until $10 (lines left) reaches 0 or the list ends. The first band uses only its visible part (-running sum). Each band calls ParallaxApplyScrollOffset, writes count bytes of at most $7F lines and stores the accumulator >> 4, sign-extended from bit 11, as the value. The 'Negative' in the name refers to the negative height words it consumes.
ParallaxWriteNegativeScrollRampY: The same loop for constant bands (size 4): value = record word +2 copied unchanged. Used by the COLDATA, CGADSUB and CGDATA entries.
ParallaxApplyScrollOffset: Computes one scroll band's value into $06 and its accumulator word. Factor <> 0: accumulator = (factor low byte x $18 / factor high byte) + base, i.e. a proportional follow of the scroll source. Factor = 0: accumulator += base + $1A, an auto-scroll.

blockNote: Entry index for parallax_thinker (Bank 01, 37 word pointers, $00-$24). The spawn-record parameter byte of the thinker is the index. Each pointer addresses one entry blob: buffer address (word, bank $7E), bank byte, config byte, record size, then records. The format and the decoded contents of every used entry are in the parallax_thinker block note.
The header bytes are NOT a BG mode / layer setting. Config bits 0-5 are the B-bus register index the HDMA channel writes, bit 6 multiplies the camera delta by 16 and bit 7 swaps the scroll sources.
Entries $09, $0C, $0D and $0F-$1A are bare $FFFF words (unused). Types $09 and $19 share one $FFFF word.

blockNote: Composite block of HDMA configuration tables and ramp motion curves (121022-121201, Bank 01). Parts: hdma_channel_config (64 bytes, the DMAP transfer mode per B-bus register), parallax_speed_config (13 bytes, of which entries 00-02 are the HDMA entry stride per transfer mode) and the two ramp arc curves behind ramp_motion_curves (64 and 32 frames). The parts are unrelated except for sharing the block; the name hdma_ramp_tables only describes them as a group.

parallax_speed_config: HDMA entry stride (count byte + data bytes) indexed by the DMAP transfer mode: mode 0 = 2, modes 1 and 2 = 3. ParallaxResolveChannelSpeed (parallax_thinker) looks up hdma_channel_config[register index] & 7 and stores the result in DP $04, where the band writers use it to step the buffer write pointer. It is a stride, not a scroll speed. Only entries 00-02 ($02, $03, $03) are reachable because every config byte has a low-3-bit value of 0-2; entries 03-0C ($05, $05, $64, $00, then $FF / $7F pairs) have no reader (the FF 7F pattern resembles HDMA line-count data, inferred).

blockNote: Inventory-screen BG3 vertical-scroll HDMA (Bank 00, 48016-48022). A type-B thinker (filter word $0804, so it runs right after ResetHdmaState every frame) that does nothing but bind one HDMA channel to a fixed 7-entry table. It is spawned by the inventory overlay scene $FF.

COP [QueueDma] ( @dma_channel_00BB97, #12 ): the second operand is the B-bus register index, $12 = $2112 BG3VOFS (transfer mode 2, written twice for the low and high byte). It is not a byte count. QueueDma goes through SetupHdmaChannel_Direct.

The table (dma_channel_00BB97, 21 bytes) is {count, low, high} per entry: lines 0-111 V = 0, then 48 lines V = 0, then four 12-line bands with V = $0B, $0F, $13, $17, then 64 lines V = $20. The line counts add to 272, more than a frame, so no terminator is needed. From line 160 down BG3's vertical scroll steps up from 0 to $20 (visual result not checked).
Earlier notes called this a '12-byte DMA table to VRAM'; that was wrong.

code_00BB90: Binds the BG3VOFS table and returns. Re-run every frame because ResetHdmaState clears the channel assignment.
dma_channel_00BB97: Direct-mode HDMA table for BG3VOFS: seven {line count, scroll value low, scroll value high} entries (111+48 lines at 0, 12 lines each at $0B / $0F / $13 / $17, then 64 lines at $20). The line counts are shown in the data lines as the first operand.

blockNote: Unused debug actor (Bank 0B, 784986-785010): sets four player stats to $0040 and kills itself. Nothing in extracted/ spawns it - it is in no scene_actors list and no script spawn - so it is dead code kept in the ROM.

The four writes are playerStr, playerDef, playerMaxHp and hpToHeal, all $0040 (64). It does not touch playerHp, so the player's current HP only rises through the heal request. For comparison debug_man sets HP 40 / STR 127 / DEF 127 (plus the ability mask and a warp menu) and unused_debug_mode sets HP 19 / STR 32 / DEF 33.

The WRAM map describes hpToHeal as a heal request that the HUD plays out as the HP recovery animation; no reader of $0B22 was found in extracted/, so that is documentation only (see the questions file).

785007.text: Heal request of 64 (HP recovery animation per the WRAM map); playerHp itself is not written
